ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Alexander the Great Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Establishing care for left chest wall pain and breathlessness on exertion since an old penetrating chest wound, with heavy episodic drinking and recent bereavement found at the visit: chest X-ray, spirometry, liver tests, PEth, AUDIT, PHQ-9, safety assessment, and a pulmonology consultation. Concerns: Pain at the old chest wound and breathlessness that slow him on the march; He wants to drink less at banquets without giving up his officers' company; Grief for his closest companion, and poor sleep since. [S]

tr.td: Acetaminophen 500 mg oral tablet, one or two tablets up to four times a day as needed for chest wall pain, no more than 2,000 mg in a day while he is drinking heavily
One to two tablets by mouth every six hours as needed; no more than four tablets a day
Thiamine 100 mg oral tablet once daily for three months
Lidocaine 5% medicated patch, one patch over the painful scar for up to 12 hours in each 24 hours
Apply one patch to the painful area for up to 12 hours, then remove for 12 hours

Chest X-ray, PA and lateral: smooth pleural thickening along the left lateral and posterior lower chest with blunting of the left costophrenic angle; healed fracture of the left fifth rib anterolaterally; no pneumothorax, effusion or radio-opaque foreign body; lungs otherwise clear; heart and mediastinum normal
Spirometry before bronchodilator, ATS/ERS 2019 acceptability and repeatability met

CT of the chest without contrast: localized pleural thickening up to 7 mm over the left lateral and posterior lower chest with a thin rim of calcification, consistent with an old organized hemothorax; a linear subpleural scar along the wound track in the left lower lobe with slight volume loss; healed fracture of the left fifth rib with callus; no retained metallic or other foreign body; no bronchopleural fistula, loculated fluid, empyema, nodule or emphysema; right lung normal
Lung volumes by body plethysmography and single-breath diffusing capacity
Six-minute walk test on a 30-meter course
Irrigation and simple repair of a 4 cm laceration of the left forearm under local anesthetic (lidocaine 1%), six interrupted nylon sutures
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes

list.item: Left chest wall pain at the scar of an old penetrating arrow wound, with breathlessness on exertion and a reduced FVC (78 percent predicted) with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio, and heavy episodic drinking (AUDIT 19, PEth 236 ng/mL), found at intake; cause and extent under evaluation with a pulmonology consultation and an addiction medicine assessment: resolved, confirmed [S]

Chronic post-traumatic chest wall pain: intercostal neuropathic pain at the healed left chest wound and fifth rib fracture, with tenderness and a small area of allodynia over the scar: active, confirmed [S]

Localized left pleural thickening (fibrothorax) from an old organized hemothorax after a penetrating chest wound, with a mild restrictive defect (TLC 79 percent predicted) and normal gas transfer; no retained foreign body, fistula or trapped lung on CT: active, confirmed [S]

Alcohol use disorder, mild (three DSM-5-TR criteria): drinking more than intended at banquets, riding after drinking, and arguments with his officers while drunk; ten or more drinks on two or three nights a week, more since his bereavement; no withdrawal; AUDIT 19; PEth 236 ng/mL: active, confirmed [S]

Bereavement five months after the death of his closest companion since boyhood, with depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 12, item 9 scored 0) that do not meet criteria for a major depressive episode; prolonged grief disorder cannot be diagnosed before twelve months: active, confirmed [S]
Laceration of the left forearm, 4 cm, from a practice blade in a training drill; clean edges, no tendon, nerve or vessel injury; repaired with sutures; healed: resolved, confirmed [S]

tr.td: Establishing care for left chest wall pain and breathlessness on exertion since an old penetrating chest wound, with heavy episodic drinking and recent bereavement found at the visit: chest X-ray, spirometry, liver tests, PEth, AUDIT, PHQ-9, safety assessment, and a pulmonology consultation

Two-week review, seen the same day by pulmonology and by the clinic's addiction medicine clinician: CT of the chest, lung volumes, gas transfer and six-minute walk; chest wall pain plan; DSM-5-TR assessment and a drinking goal
Six-week review: chest wall pain and the exercise program, drinking and PEth, liver tests, grief and mood, safety, and the healed forearm wound
Nine-week review: repeat spirometry, pain, drinking and PEth, AUDIT-C, mood, safety and the plan ahead
Same-day sick visit for a left forearm laceration
Periodic adult preventive visit, with travel and campaign health

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Chest: chest X-ray and spirometry at intake; CT of the chest and lung volumes with diffusing capacity and a six-minute walk at the consultation; repeat spirometry after two to three months of the exercise program

Pulmonology consultation for chest wall pain and reduced lung function after a penetrating chest wound: a retained fragment, pleural thickening or trapped lung, the need for surgery, pain treatment without opioids, fitness for heavy exertion, and lung function follow-up
Chest wall pain: acetaminophen up to 2,000 mg a day; no opioids, tramadol, gabapentinoids or benzodiazepines while he drinks heavily; no regular anti-inflammatory tablets with heavy drinking
Lidocaine 5% patch over the scar for up to 12 hours a day; an intercostal nerve block if pain stays above 4 of 10 after six weeks; a four-week telephone check on the patch

Exercise and breathing program: physical therapy for thoracic mobility and scar desensitization, deep-breathing exercises, and graded aerobic and strength training back to long marches; no decortication, which is kept for a trapped lung or severe restriction

Alcohol: AUDIT, DSM-5-TR criteria and PEth with consent; liver tests; brief counseling at intake and sessions with the clinic's addiction medicine clinician; withdrawal risk assessed (no withdrawal expected with his pattern); thiamine for three months; PEth and liver tests at follow-up

Drinking goal chosen with him for a mild alcohol use disorder: no more than four drinks on any day and fourteen in a week, two alcohol-free days a week, water between drinks at banquets, and no riding or driving after drinking; naltrexone offered and declined, to be offered again if the goal is not met

Grief and mood: sessions with the clinic's behavioral health clinician, sleep routine, PHQ-9 every four to six weeks; reassess for prolonged grief disorder only if intense grief persists beyond twelve months; antidepressant only if a major depressive episode develops

Safety: a structured safety assessment, the service pistol kept in the armory off duty and never carried after drinking, a written safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and safety review at every visit

Travel and campaign health for months in Mesopotamia: no malaria chemoprophylaxis where CDC lists no transmission, reviewed before any other travel; insect and tick precautions; safe food and water; hepatitis A and typhoid vaccines; rabies pre-exposure vaccination offered
Find out why the old wound still hurts and why he is breathless, and whether anything remains in the chest
Post-traumatic intercostal pain and a localized fibrothorax with mild restriction; no retained fragment, fistula or trapped lung; no surgery needed
Chest wall pain 3 of 10 or less on exertion, without opioids
6 to 2 of 10 on the lidocaine patch, acetaminophen and the exercise program
Back to long marches and runs without stopping for breath
Six-minute walk 548 m at the consultation; FVC 78 to 83 percent predicted; running again at nine weeks
No more than four drinks on any day and fourteen in a week, no riding or driving after drinking, and two or more alcohol-free days a week
PEth 236 to 31 ng/mL; within his limits at all but one banquet
Sleep seven hours, and room to grieve

list.item: Independent; marches and rides, but breathless and in pain at the scar on long climbs and when carrying heavy kit; cannot run as far as a year ago [S]

Alert, direct and engaged; speech normal; mood 'heavy'; affect sad when he speaks of his companion, otherwise full; no psychotic symptoms; no thoughts of suicide or of harming anyone; insight and judgment good; PHQ-9 12 with item 9 scored 0; GAD-7 6 [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 2026-03-09: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. Outpatient care with close follow-up. Risk factors reviewed without detail: recent bereavement, depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 12), heavy episodic drinking, chronic pain, and access to a service weapon. The service pistol stays in the unit armory off duty and he will not carry it after drinking; he will not ride or drive after drinking. A written safety plan was made with him, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988) and the clinic's number were written on a card he carries. Safety is reviewed at every visit [S]
